newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude slightly higher, Tapis supported.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude slightly higher, Tapis supported.

text.p: Asian crude prices were marginally higher on Friday in quiet trading with Tapis generally well supported.
The March swaps were quoted at $21.90/$22.10 in Asia's afternoon, 30 cents higher than a day-earlier.

The paper was partly supported by the loss of Cossack crude production. Operator Woodside confirmed Friday that production was cut to 40,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) -- a cut that could stay in place until mid March -- because of production problems.
Some players have also been closing out a lot of positions on Tapis swaps and positons related to hedges on Tapis.
A decline in Brent and NYMEX crude in past week and prompted players to switch or close their position.
Otherwise, players said there was a perception that light sweet grades would hold up better in March than their heavy sweet counterparts.
Several West African imports and the closure for maintenance of the Dumai refinery was likely to undermine the heavier grades, like Minas.
Minas was being offered at ICP +60 cents compared with last done in February of ICP +75 cents. Traders said there were no bids seen yet for the Indonesian key grade.
In addition, operators were waiting for export allocations, which are expected to be announced by Pertamina sometime early next week.
A March Belida, traded between a Japanese trader and a U.S. major at ICP +70/80 cents, is said to have been the only Indonesian grade that has traded so far for March.
Traders said they expected trading to get underway next week for April MidEast grades and March regional grades.
